full_text_en:
Wuxi Guowei Ceramic Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. and Jiang Guoping v. Changshu Linzhi Electric Heating Device Co., Ltd. and Suning Commerce Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent

【Ruling Summary】

When calculating the amount of damages for patent infringement based on the profits gained by the infringer through the infringement, depending on the claims of the parties and the facts of the case, for an accused infringing product comprising multiple components or multiple patents, in principle, it is not advisable to simply calculate the infringing profits by multiplying the total sales amount of the infringing product by the profit margin of the infringing product. Rather, the contribution of the patent in suit to the profit of the infringing product should be considered, and the calculation should be made using the method of "total sales amount of the infringing product x profit margin x contribution of the patented technology to the product value." The contribution of the patented technology to the product value may be determined by taking into account factors such as the importance of the patent in suit to the product.

Where the infringing acts are separable, when calculating damages for infringement, if there are both parts where the loss of the right holder or the profit of the infringer can be calculated with relative precision, and parts where such calculation is difficult, the former part may be compensated based on the loss of the right holder or the profit of the infringer, and the latter part may be compensated by statutory damages. The amount of damages shall be the sum of the two.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2018) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 111

Re-Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Wuxi Guowei Ceramic Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. Domicile: Tongshu West Road, Dingshu Town, Yixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Guoping, General Manager of the Company.

Re-Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Jiang Guoping, male, born on May 21, 1955, Han Chinese, domiciled in Yixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Jointly Authorized Agents ad litem of the Two Re-Applicants: Bai Shangchun, male, born on April 23, 1962, Han Chinese, patent agent of Nanjing Sugao Patent & Trademark Agency, domiciled in Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Jointly Authorized Agents ad litem of the Two Re-Applicants: Kang Yanwen, lawyer of Jiangsu Sugao Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Changshu Linzhi Electric Heating Device Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 88 Tonglin Road, High-tech Park, Changshu Economic and Technological Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: He Zheng'an, Chairman of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Respondent at Second Instance): Suning Commerce Group Co., Ltd. (formerly Suning Cloud Business Group Co., Ltd.). Domicile: Floors 1-5, Jinshan Building, No. 8 Shanxi Road, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Jindong, Chairman of the Company.

Authorized Agent ad litem: Zheng Fangyan, female, employee of the Company.

Re-Applicants Wuxi Guowei Ceramic Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guowei Company) and Jiang Guoping, in the case of dispute over infringement of utility model patent with Respondents Changshu Linzhi Electric Heating Device Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Linzhi Company) and Respondent Suning Commerce Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Suning Company), disagreed with the civil judgment (2016) Su Min Zhong No. 105 of the Jiangsu High People's Court and applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered the civil ruling (2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 2638 on December 21, 2017, granting the retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law, appointed Wang Dong as a technical investigator to participate in the litigation activities of this case, and held a public hearing of this case. Jiang Guoping appeared in person; the jointly authorized agents ad litem of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping, Bai Shangchun and Kang Yanwen, and the authorized agent ad litem of Suning Company, Zheng Fangyan, appeared in court. Linzhi Company, having been summoned by subpoena of this Court, failed to appear without justifiable reasons; this Court conducted the trial by default according to law. This case is now concluded.

Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping applied for retrial, claiming that the judgment of the second instance had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law, and that this case falls under item (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and should be retried. The main reasons are: (1) The introduction of "implied technical features" in the judgment of the second instance violates the doctrine of complete coverage, narrows the scope of protection of claim 2 of the patent in suit of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping, and lacks legal basis. (2) The interpretation of claim 2 of the patent in suit in the judgment of the second instance is erroneous. The phrase "the heat dissipation aluminum strips (11) are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1) in the heating core (10)" in claim 2 of the patent in suit is a clerical error; the only interpretation of this claim should be that the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the "upper and lower surfaces" of the heat-conducting aluminum tube in the heating core. However, the above interpretation does not require that "the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube in claim 2 of the patent must have grooves, and the function of the grooves is to ensure that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation aluminum strips." The functions of providing grooves on the left and right side surfaces and on the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube are different, and there is no necessary connection between the two. Based on the above reasons, Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping requested this Court: 1. To revoke the civil judgment (2016) Su Min Zhong No. 105 of the Jiangsu High People's Court; 2. To amend the judgment to find that Linzhi Company's infringement is established and to support all claims of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping in the first instance, i.e., to order Linzhi Company to compensate Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 15 million; 3. To order Linzhi Company to bear all litigation costs of the first and second instances.

Linzhi Company submitted its opinion, stating that the reasons for retrial of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping are untenable and should be rejected. The main reasons are: (1) Claim 2 of the patent in suit has an implied technical feature that the upper and lower surfaces have grooves. The "heat-conducting aluminum tube (1)" in claim 2 of the patent in suit uses the same identifier as the "heat-conducting aluminum tube (1)" in claim 1, and they are identical; therefore, there is essentially a reference relationship between claim 2 and claim 1. In combination with the description of grooves (4) in the specification of the patent in suit, it can be determined that the "heat-conducting aluminum tube (1)" of claim 2 has grooves on the upper and lower surfaces. Meanwhile, according to the description of the advantages of the utility model patent and the embodiments, the left and right side surfaces and the grooves on the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube must exist simultaneously, and they are mutually dependent; the "heat-conducting aluminum tube (1)" of claim 2 has the implied technical feature of grooves on the upper and lower surfaces. (2) The phrase in claim 2 of the patent in suit regarding heat dissipation aluminum strips being adhered to the "left and right side surfaces" of the heat-conducting aluminum tube in the heating core is not a clerical error. According to the specification, adhering the heat dissipation aluminum strips to the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube in the heating core is only a preferred solution, not the only solution. Moreover, there is no situation in this case where the heat dissipation aluminum strips cannot be adhered in a semicircular groove. Adhering the heat dissipation aluminum strips to the surface with greater contact with the heating core is more conducive to heat dissipation; whether to adhere to the upper and lower surfaces or the left and right side surfaces should be determined based on the position of the heat-conducting aluminum tube and its contact surface with the heating core. (3) The accused infringing product in this case does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 2 of the patent in suit. The accused infringing product has multiple technical features that are neither identical nor equivalent to those of claim 2. The accused infringing product's heat-conducting aluminum tube does not have grooves on its upper and lower surfaces; the side grooves of the heat-conducting aluminum tube are not semicircular and are formed before pressing, which differs from the corresponding technical features of claim 2 of the patent in suit in terms of process, effect, etc.; the heat dissipation fins are not bonded but fixed by wedge groove pressing, and the heat dissipation fins are not installed on the left and right side surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube, and their width is smaller than the width of the heat-conducting aluminum tube.

Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province (Court of First Instance), requesting the court to order: 1. Linzhi Company to immediately cease the infringing acts and destroy the infringing products; Suning Company to cease selling the air conditioner units containing the accused infringing products; 2. Linzhi Company to compensate Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 15 million; 3. Linzhi Company to bear all litigation costs of the case.

The Court of First Instance found the following main facts:

(I) Status of rights of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping

On September 8, 2009, Jiang Guoping filed an application for a utility model patent entitled "A heat-conducting aluminum tube of a PTC heater and a PTC heater" with the State Intellectual Property Office. On June 2, 2010, the State Intellectual Property Office granted the utility model patent right, with patent number ZL200920230829.5 (i.e., the patent in suit). On June 23, 2010, Jiang Guoping and Guowei Company entered into a licensing agreement, authorizing Guowei Company to exclusively exploit the patent in suit, with the contract valid until the expiration date of the patent term. It was also agreed that in the event of infringement by a third party, Guowei Company had the right to exercise litigation rights separately or jointly with Jiang Guoping.

During the first instance trial, Linzhi Company filed a request for invalidation with the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office. On October 9, 2014, the Patent Reexamination Board issued the Invalidation Request Examination Decision No. 24085 (hereinafter referred to as Decision No. 24085), declaring part of the claims of the patent in suit invalid. The valid claim 1 maintained is: A heat-conducting aluminum tube of a PTC heater, the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1) having a cavity (2) with two open ends, characterized in that: the upper surface and lower surface of the heat-conducting aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves (4), and the wall thickness of the aluminum tube (3) is 0mm-1.5mm. Claim 2 is: A PTC heater, comprising a heating core (10) and heat dissipation aluminum strips (11), characterized in that: the heating core (10) is formed by pressing ceramic PTC heating elements (5), insulating ceramic sheets (6), conductive electrodes (7), and an insulating layer (8) through the rear cavity of the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1); the heat dissipation aluminum strips (11) are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1) in the heating core (10); the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1), after pressing, forms semicircular grooves (9) on the left side surface and the right side surface, respectively. Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping clarified that the scope of protection they seek is claim 2 as maintained after the invalidation review.

(II) Status of Linzhi Company, Suning Company, and the accused infringing acts

On October 18, 2013, notary personnel Yuan Junhuan and Xu Xianming from Yixing Notary Public Office, Jiangsu Province, together with Yue Qing and Wu Jie, authorized agents of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping, came to a Suning appliance store on Zhongda Street, Lishui District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province. The agents Yue Qing purchased one TCL air conditioner, one Hisense air conditioner, and one Midea air conditioner (including indoor units and outdoor units) from the store and immediately obtained three special invoices for value-added tax of Jiangsu Province and three deduction slips for each air conditioner. The total price for the TCL air conditioner was RMB 1,699, the Hisense air conditioner was RMB 2,799, and the Midea air conditioner was RMB 2,299. After the purchase, the above personnel brought the air conditioners and invoices to the Yixing Notary Public Office. In the parking lot of the notary office, air conditioner maintenance personnel disassembled the indoor units of the purchased air conditioners. Notary Yuan Junhuan sealed the extracted PTC heaters and affixed the seal of the notary office. Notary Yuan Junhuan took 36 photos of the purchase site, the purchased goods, and the disassembly site. The entire process was conducted under the on-site supervision of Notary Yuan Junhuan and notary assistant Xu Xianming. The Yixing Notary Public Office issued the notarial certificate No. (2013) Xi Yi Zheng Jing Nei Zi No. 2592. Linzhi Company confirmed that the PTC heaters in the TCL and other air conditioners purchased by notarization were products it sold.

The accused infringing product was compared with the patent in suit. Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin argued that the phrase "the heat dissipation aluminum strips (11) are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1) in the heating core (10)" in claim 2 is a clerical error; from the specification and drawings, it should be "upper and lower surfaces." The accused infringing product has grooves on the left and right side surfaces, and there is a pressing process; claim 2 does not limit that only left-right pressing falls within the scope of protection. Moreover, even if there is a slight depression on the left and right side surfaces before pressing, it does not affect the accused infringing product falling within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. The grooves on the left and right side surfaces are intended to absorb excess extension during pressing, making the product structure more compact; the shape is not very important. The accused infringing product also contains all other technical features of claim 2 and falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit.

Linzhi Company argued that: 1. It does not agree that there is a clerical error in the claims. The scope of protection of the patent should be based on the claims; if the claims can clearly express the meaning, there is no need to refer to the specification and embodiments for interpretation. Moreover, paragraph [0008] of the specification clearly states "left and right side surfaces"; the specification provides a preferred technical solution, and the drawings also show a preferred solution. Therefore, the argument of a clerical error by Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin cannot stand. 2. The grooves on the left and right side surfaces of the accused infringing product are pre-formed; there is a clear gap between the left and right side surfaces of the aluminum tube and the heating core; the middle part of the upper and lower surfaces in contact with the heating chip is slightly raised. From this, it can be seen that the pressing position of the heater should be at the four corners of the aluminum tube, the purpose of which is to press the upper and lower surfaces of the aluminum tube tightly against the heating core for better contact, rather than to form semicircular grooves. The function of the grooves in the accused infringing product is inconsistent with the function of the semicircular grooves in the patent in suit. The grooves in the accused infringing product are consistent with the technical features disclosed in utility model patent document No. 200620034186.3. 3. The grooves on the accused infringing product are not semicircular, and the grooves have various shapes such as U-shaped, V-shaped, W-shaped, etc. Therefore, the accused infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of claim 2 of the patent in suit as claimed by Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin.

Linzhi Company admitted in court that the aluminum tube and the heating core inside the aluminum tube are tightly connected, and there is a pressing process, but what is pressed in the accused infringing product are the four corners of the aluminum tube.

Both parties agreed that the PTC heaters obtained by the Court of First Instance through evidence preservation from Linzhi Company, TCL Air Conditioner (Zhongshan) Co., Ltd., and Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioner Co., Ltd. are substantially consistent in structure with the above products.

(III) Defense of Linzhi Company

Linzhi Company argued that the technical features of the accused infringing product are disclosed in utility model patent document No. 200620034186.3, i.e., the grooves in the accused infringing product are pre-formed; the product in this case uses existing technology and does not constitute infringement. Meanwhile, during the invalidation phase of the patent in suit, Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin emphasized that the grooves being formed by pressing is a technical feature of the patent in suit to maintain its validity, but the accused infringing product in this case does not include this technical feature.

Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin argued that, first, the utility model patent No. 200620034186.3 had been compared in Decision No. 24085, and a clear conclusion was reached to maintain the validity of the patent in suit. Second, the "U-shaped" grooves disclosed in utility model patent No. 200620034186.3 are not formed by pressing, which is different from the semicircular grooves formed by pressing in the patent in suit.

(IV) Other facts found

Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin claimed that, based on (1) the investigation records made by the Court of First Instance at Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd., a material coding list issued by Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd., and the supply agreement between Midea and Linzhi Company; (2) the investigation records made by the Court of First Instance at TCL Air Conditioner (Zhongshan) Co., Ltd., material coding list, copy of contract, etc.; (3) a statement issued by the Procurement Department of Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioner Co., Ltd.; (4) investigation records made by the agents of Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin, authorization letters, replies to investigation orders, summary tables, notarial certificate No. (2015) Yang You Zheng Min Nei Zi No. 992, and physical evidence, etc., it was confirmed that Linzhi Company had sold the accused infringing products in the amount of RMB 160 million. Linzhi Company argued that the product models in the two material coding lists are different from the product models of the physical accused infringing products and cannot be considered to have the same structure as the product in this case; the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the statement issued by Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioner Co., Ltd. cannot be recognized, and the statement did not specify what product was supplied, which is irrelevant to this case; the summary table was only signed by Liu Zhongkai and Zhao Sheng, without the company seal and the signature of the legal representative, and its three characteristics (authenticity, legality, relevance) are not recognized; at the same time, it cannot be shown whether the products in the summary table fall within the scope of protection of the patent.

Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin also provided a "Report on the verification of the 2014 enterprise information disclosure of Wuxi Guowei Ceramic Electric Appliance Co., Ltd." issued by Yixing Zhengda Tax Agency. Guowei Company and Jiang Guopin claimed that the report confirmed that the profit margin of the patented products produced by Guowei Company was over 30%, and considering Linzhi Company's sales amount, the claimed compensation amount was reasonable. Linzhi Company disputed the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the report.

To prove that the accused infringing products it sold had a legal source, Suning Company provided the contract and invoices for its procurement of the TCL air conditioners in this case. Since Guowei Company, Jiang Guopin, and Linzhi Company recognized the authenticity and purpose of proof of this set of evidence, the fact that Suning Company's sold accused infringing products had a legal source was confirmed.

First Instance Court held: (1) Regarding the interpretation of Patent Claim 2. The phrase "the left and right side faces" in "the heat-dissipating aluminum strips (11) are attached to the left and right side faces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1) in the heating core (10)" in Patent Claim 2 is a clerical error and should read "the upper and lower surfaces." (2) The accused infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of Patent Claim 2. The grooves on the left and right side faces of the accused infringing product, after being pressed, further deform, inevitably absorbing the extension in the width direction of the aluminum tube during the pressing process, thereby making the product structure more compact, which embodies the technical features of Patent Claim 2. Whether the grooves on the left and right side faces of the accused infringing product are strictly semicircular grooves does not affect the inventive function of the heat-conducting aluminum tube in clamping the heating element to improve heat dissipation performance. Therefore, the accused infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of Patent Claim 2. (3) Regarding civil liability. Linzhi Company shall immediately cease the infringing act, destroy the infringing products, and Suning Company shall immediately cease selling air conditioner units containing the infringing product. As the evidence submitted by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping cannot prove that all products sold by Linzhi Company are the accused infringing products, nor can it prove the profits obtained by Linzhi Company, and at the same time, the evidence provided by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping also cannot prove the losses they suffered due to Linzhi Company's production and sale of the infringing products, the specific amount of damages shall be determined at RMB 1,000,000 based on factors such as the scope of compensation claimed by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping, the general sales price and profit margin of PTC heater products, the duration of Linzhi Company's sales, the nature of the infringing act, and the reasonable expenses incurred by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping to stop the infringement. In summary, in accordance with Article 11, Paragraph 1, Article 59, Paragraph 1, and Article 65 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the First Instance Court rendered the following judgment: 1. Linzhi Company shall immediately cease the production and sale of products infringing the patent rights of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping in this case, and shall immediately destroy the infringing products in stock; 2. Suning Company shall immediately cease the sale of air conditioner units containing the patent-infringing product; 3. Linzhi Company shall, within ten days of the judgment becoming effective, compensate Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 1,000,000; 4. All other claims of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping are dismissed. The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 111,800 shall be borne by Linzhi Company.

Guowei Company, Jiang Guoping, and Linzhi Company all appealed against the judgment to the Jiangsu High People's Court (Second Instance Court). Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping requested the court to set aside item 3 of the first instance judgment and instead enter a judgment ordering Linzhi Company to compensate them for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 15,000,000, and to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Their main facts and reasons were: The determination of the amount of damages in the first instance judgment was extremely simplistic, failing to provide a detailed analysis of the relevant evidence materials concerning the infringing product, and the relevant evidence submitted by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping and the damage claims based thereon were not accepted or supported, without providing convincing and sufficient reasons.

Linzhi Company requested the court to set aside the first instance judgment, dismiss all claims of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping, and order Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Its main facts and reasons were: (1) The accused infringing product differs from the patent in suit in many respects: 1. The upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube of the accused infringing product do not have the grooves (4) for offsetting the dimensional extension caused by pressing as specified in Patent Claim 1. 2. The accused infringing product does not have the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1) described in Patent Claim 2. 3. The heat-dissipating aluminum strips of the accused infringing product are fixed on the upper and lower surfaces by brazing or through wedge slots on the heat-conducting aluminum tube, not on the left and right side faces as described in Patent Claim 2. 4. The grooves on the left and right side faces of the accused infringing product were not formed after pressing, but were formed before pressing, and the groove shape is an inverted "V-shaped" groove or a "U-shaped" groove, which differs from the semicircular groove in the patent in terms of the timing of formation and function. 5. Patent Claim 2 has an implicit technical feature that "the width of the heat-conducting aluminum tube is consistent with the width of the heat-dissipating aluminum strip," but in the accused infringing product, the widths are inconsistent. (2) The first instance judgment erroneously found that "the heat-dissipating aluminum strips are attached to the left and right side faces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube" in Patent Claim 2 was a clerical error. (3) The first instance judgment's analysis of the function of the grooves on the upper and lower surfaces and the semicircular grooves on the left and right side faces is inconsistent with the description in the patent specification, constituting an error in fact-finding. (4) The first instance judgment erroneously equated the "clamping" of the accused infringing product with the "pressing" in Claim 2, which is an error in fact-finding. (5) The first instance judgment's opinion that Linzhi Company raised a prior art defense is inconsistent with the facts. In the first instance, Linzhi Company cited evidence 5 from the invalidation decision to prove that the U-shaped grooves of the accused infringing product differ from the semicircular grooves of the patent in suit, which was a non-infringement defense. (6) During the invalidation proceeding, the patentee of the patent in suit made a narrowing interpretation of the claims, i.e., emphasizing the differences and advantages of the semicircular grooves of the patent in suit compared to the U-shaped grooves in the prior art, which was adopted by the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office. The doctrine of estoppel should apply in this case, and the semicircular grooves of the patent in suit should be interpreted consistently with the patentee's statements made during the invalidation proceeding. According to such interpretation, the U-shaped grooves of the accused infringing product are inconsistent with the technical feature of the semicircular grooves of the patent in suit.

The Second Instance Court additionally found: The upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube of the accused infringing product are smooth, and at the left and right sides of the upper and lower surfaces, a pair of inwardly closing flashes are provided, so that the upper and lower parts of the cross-section of the heat-conducting aluminum tube form a dovetail groove. The flashes on both sides clamp the edges of the heat-dissipating aluminum strips, thereby fixing and pressing the heat-dissipating aluminum strips against the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube. The grooves on the left and right side faces of the accused infringing product are inverted "V-shaped" grooves and "U-shaped" grooves. The width of the heat-dissipating aluminum strips is narrower than the width of the heat-conducting aluminum tube.

The Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office made Decision No. 24085 on October 9, 2014. Regarding the issue in Patent Claim 2 that the heat-dissipating aluminum strips are attached to the left and right side faces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube, the decision held: "Under the current limitation of Claim 2, after the heat-conducting aluminum tube is pressed, semicircular grooves are formed on the left and right side faces, which cannot form a flat surface, making it impossible to attach heat-dissipating aluminum strips in a semicircular groove; i.e., the above technical feature of Claim 2 is obviously contradictory. Paragraph [0006] of the specification of the patent in suit states that grooves are respectively provided on the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube of the PTC heater; paragraph [0007] states that after pressing the heat-conducting aluminum tube, semicircular grooves are formed on the left and right side faces; paragraph [0010] states that the grooves on the surface of the aluminum tube and the semicircular grooves on the side faces of the aluminum tube's heating core offset the extension in the width direction of the aluminum tube, ensuring that the width of the heating core aluminum tube after pressing is consistent with the width of the heat-dissipating strips. It can be seen that the semicircular grooves on the left and right side faces are for clamping the heating core, and the grooves on the upper and lower surfaces of the aluminum tube are for ensuring that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat-dissipating strips. Based on this, it is clear that the heat-dissipating strips should obviously be attached to the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube, not the left and right side faces. Figure 4 of the specification of the patent in suit also supports this conclusion. That is, according to the description of the specification, the obviously contradictory features in Claim 2 can be understood uniquely and correctly, and they should be 'the heat-dissipating aluminum strips are attached to the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube in the heating core.' This clarifies the scope of protection of Claim 2, and the following evaluation of inventiveness is based on this scope of protection."

The Second Instance Court held: (1) Regarding the interpretation of the patent claims in suit. Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping argued that the phrase "the left and right side faces" in "the heat-dissipating aluminum strips (11) are attached to the left and right side faces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube (1) in the heating core (10)" in Claim 2 is a clerical error and should be understood as "upper and lower surfaces." Decision No. 24085, in conjunction with the relevant content of the specification of the patent in suit, determined that "according to the description of the specification, the obviously contradictory features in Claim 2 can be understood uniquely and correctly, and they should be 'the heat-dissipating aluminum strips are attached to the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube in the heating core.'" This determination shall serve as the basis for interpreting Claim 2. The basis for reinterpreting ambiguous content in the claims must be strictly limited to the scope of the claims, specification, and drawings. Furthermore, during the reasoning process for clarification or correction interpretation, those relevant technical features that are cited, appear in the claims, specification, and drawings, and serve as prerequisites and intermediate conditions for reasoning, shall be considered implicit technical features and shall have a limiting effect on the claims after clarification or correction. In this case, during the process of making a correction interpretation regarding the attachment position of the heat-dissipating aluminum strips in Claim 2, Decision No. 24085 held: "the semicircular grooves on the left and right side faces are for clamping the heating core, and the grooves on the upper and lower surfaces of the aluminum tube are for ensuring that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat-dissipating strips" and concluded: "Based on this, it is clear that the heat-dissipating strips should obviously be attached to the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube, not the left and right side faces." Therefore, the premise for Decision No. 24085 to identify the text "left and right side faces" in Claim 2 regarding the attachment position of the heat-dissipating aluminum strips as a clerical error and correct it to "upper and lower surfaces" is that the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube in Patent Claim 2 must have grooves, and the function of these grooves is to ensure that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat-dissipating aluminum strips. Without this premise, the correction of the clerical error from "left and right side faces" to "upper and lower surfaces" in Patent Claim 2 would lack a basis for reasoning. Therefore, although Patent Claim 2 does not include the technical feature "the upper surface and lower surface of the heat-conducting aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves," since during the correction interpretation of the textual ambiguity in Claim 2, "the upper surface and lower surface of the heat-conducting aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves" and their function served as a premise for reasoning, they should be considered implicit technical features of Claim 2, and the limiting effect of this technical feature on the scope of protection of Claim 2 must be considered. (2) Regarding the technical comparison between the accused infringing product and the patent claims. Although Claim 2 of the patent in suit does not directly limit the heat-conducting aluminum tube to having grooves on the upper and lower surfaces, due to the correction interpretation, it is necessary to consider the limiting effect of the technical feature "the upper surface and lower surface of the heat-conducting aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves." Since the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube of the accused infringing product do not have grooves, and because the grooves in the patent in suit are not dispensable but have the function of "ensuring that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat-dissipating strips," the accused infringing product lacks the implicit technical feature of Patent Claim 2: that the upper and lower surfaces of the heat-conducting aluminum tube also have grooves, and the function of these grooves is to ensure that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat-dissipating aluminum strips. Therefore, according to the "all-element rule," the accused infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of Patent Claim 2. In summary, the acts of Linzhi Company in manufacturing and selling, and Suning Company in selling the accused infringing product do not constitute infringement of the patent rights of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping in this case, and Linzhi Company and Suning Company are not required to bear civil liability. In accordance with Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases, Article 4 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases, and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Second Instance Court rendered the following judgment: 1. Set aside the civil judgment (2013) Ning Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 510 of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province; 2. Dismiss all claims of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping. The first instance and second instance case acceptance fees of RMB 111,800 each shall be borne by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping.
