On August 21, 2014, the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office conducted an oral hearing regarding the invalidation request filed by Linzhi Company against the patent in suit. Page 5 of the oral hearing record of that date recorded the following statements by the patentee of the patent in suit: "The function of the grooves in Evidence 5 is different from the function of the grooves in the patent in suit. The function of the U, W, V-shaped grooves in Claims 3 and 4 of Evidence 5 is to fix components. The function of the grooves in the patent in suit is to offset the extension in the width direction of the aluminum tube during pressing. Example 2 on page 4 of the specification of Evidence 5 describes the formation of V-shaped grooves; the V-shaped grooves are already formed before pressing. For the grooves in the patent in suit, the grooves are formed only after the heat-conducting aluminum tube is pressed. In Evidence 5, grooves existed before pressing, while in the patent in suit, grooves on the left and right side faces are formed only after pressing." In the opinion statement submitted to the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office, the patentee made similar statements.

On September 28, 2014, the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office made Decision No. 24085, which records on page 11: "Evidence 5 discloses a sealed positive temperature coefficient thermistor heater, comprising a heating element, motor terminals 4, a receiving cavity 1, and finned heat sinks 11. The receiving cavity 1 and the finned heat sinks are of an integrated structure, integrally processed from aluminum profiles. The finned heat sinks are located on the outer surface of the receiving cavity, and the heating element is located in the cavity of the receiving cavity 1. On two opposite side surfaces of the receiving cavity, along the axial direction of the receiving cavity, 'V'-shaped grooves are provided. The bottom edge of the 'V'-shaped groove is recessed toward the interior of the cavity. The side surfaces where the 'V'-shaped grooves are located are perpendicular to the side surfaces where the finned heat sinks are located. By means of plastic forming, a stamping die is used to process the receiving cavity in a direction perpendicular to the surface of the 'V'-shaped groove, causing the receiving cavity to deform and contract inward, and the force is continuously adjustable, so as to ensure good and tight contact between the two metal electrode plates 6 and each PTC thermistor 8 (i.e., temperature coefficient thermistor), and good contact with the receiving cavity, thereby fully improving heat transfer efficiency and enhancing heating performance. In order to uniformly compress the heating body inside the receiving cavity, compression grooves for causing the receiving cavity to recess inward are arranged on the edges of the receiving cavity. During processing, a clamping tool is used to squeeze the edges of the receiving cavity. The edges of the receiving cavity refer to the four edges of a rectangular body. The 'V'-shaped groove may also be a 'U'-shaped groove. It can be seen that Evidence 5 discloses the feature that 'U'-shaped grooves, i.e., semi-circular grooves, are provided on both sides of the aluminum tube of the PTC heater. However, in Evidence 5, such grooves are not used to absorb the extension of the aluminum tube in the width direction during the pressing process. Since the finned heat sinks and the receiving cavity are of an integrated structure, it is impossible to perform the operation of pressing the receiving cavity from the upper and lower surfaces where the finned heat sinks are extruded. Therefore, in the structure of Evidence 5, a 'U'-shaped groove needs to be provided before pressing the aluminum tube to provide a continuously adjustable clamping force, so that after the heating element is inserted into the receiving cavity, the 'U'-shaped groove is pressed up and down to provide an up-and-down clamping force, thereby uniformly compressing the heating element in the cavity. In this patent, the semi-circular grooves on the left and right sides of the aluminum tube are formed after pressing. Therefore, when inserting the heating element into the aluminum tube, the semi-circular grooves may not be formed temporarily or only slightly recessed, so the insertion of the heating element is smoother and safer, and will not be scratched. After the semi-circular grooves are formed by pressing, the gap between the aluminum tube and the heating element is smaller, thereby eliminating the risk of loose accessories. Moreover, the provision of such semi-circular grooves allows the upper and lower surfaces of the aluminum tube to be completely consistent with the width of the heat dissipation strips after pressing. These technical effects cannot be achieved by the 'U'-shaped groove structure of Evidence 5. Therefore, the 'U'-shaped groove of Evidence 5 cannot be equivalent to the 'semi-circular groove' of this patent."

Paragraph 0010 on page 2 of the specification of this patent records the beneficial effects of the present invention, including: the technical solution of the present invention makes the product structure more compact; after pressing, the binding between various accessories is stronger, improving thermal conductivity; the fitting clearance between the accessories in the aluminum tube cavity and the inner wall of the side surface of the aluminum tube is reduced, eliminating safety hazards such as loosening of accessories caused by external forces or machine vibration during operation, thereby improving product reliability; the product has a reasonable structure, simple manufacture, convenient installation and maintenance, and safe use, etc.

This Court, upon retrial, holds that, based on the grounds for retrial application of the applicant for retrial and the facts of this case, the issues in the retrial stage are: whether the interpretation of Claim 2 of this patent in the judgment of the second instance is correct; whether the accused infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of Claim 2 of this patent; and the determination of civil liability for infringement in this case. The analysis is as follows:

(I) Whether the interpretation of Claim 2 of this patent in the judgment of the second instance is correct

This issue includes two interrelated aspects: first, whether the statement in Claim 2 that the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the "left and right side surfaces" of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core is an obvious error that can be corrected; second, whether Claim 2 should include the implicit technical feature that "the upper surface and lower surface of the thermally conductive aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves."

First, regarding whether the statement in Claim 2 that the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the "left and right side surfaces" of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core is an obvious error that can be corrected. Article 4 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases (II) provides: "If there are ambiguities in grammar, text, punctuation, diagrams, symbols, etc., in the claims, specification, or drawings, but a person of ordinary skill in the art can derive a unique understanding by reading the claims, specification, and drawings, the people's court shall determine based on that unique understanding." With reference to this provision, an obvious error that can be corrected requires two conditions: first, a person of ordinary skill in the art can recognize that there is ambiguity or error in the record or drawings of the patent application; second, a person of ordinary skill in the art can derive a unique understanding to resolve the ambiguity or error by reading the claims, specification, and drawings. In this case, Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping argued that the "left and right side surfaces" in Claim 2, which states "the heat dissipation aluminum strips (11) are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube (1) in the heating core (10)," is a clerical error and should be understood as "upper and lower surfaces." As to whether this argument can be established, this Court analyzes as follows: First, according to the technical solution described in Claim 2, after pressing, the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube form semi-circular grooves and cannot form a flat surface. Since the function of the heat dissipation aluminum strips is to conduct heat from the heating core, even if the heat dissipation aluminum strips could be adhered in semi-circular grooves, such adhesion obviously does not conform to the basic principles of heat dissipation and cannot effectively achieve the heat dissipation function. Therefore, a person of ordinary skill in the art can recognize that there is an error in stating that the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube. Second, paragraph [0008] of the specification of this patent further highlights this error and provides a hint for resolving it. Paragraph [0008] of the specification states: "The heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core; ... In order to meet the safety requirements of split air conditioners with smaller installation spaces, it is preferred to use a row of corrugated heat dissipation aluminum strips respectively adhered to the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core." The above description, after having mentioned that the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the "left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core," states in the preferred solution that the adhesion position of the heat dissipation aluminum strips is "the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core." This not only suggests an error in Claim 2 regarding the adhesion position of the heat dissipation aluminum strips but also provides a correct method for resolving the error. Finally, paragraph [0021] of the specification and the related drawings further provide the only correct answer for resolving the error. Paragraph [0021] of the specification states: "The heater shown in Figure 4 is formed by adhering corrugated heat dissipation strips having a width consistent with the surface to the upper and lower surfaces of the heating core 10 provided with grooves." Meanwhile, Figures 4 and 6 show that the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core. Therefore, the heat dissipation aluminum strips should obviously be adhered to the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube, not the left and right side surfaces. The statement "the heat dissipation aluminum strips (11) are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube (1) in the heating core (10)" in Claim 2 of this patent is indeed a clerical error for "upper and lower surfaces" and constitutes an obvious error that can be corrected.

Second, regarding whether Claim 2 should include the implicit technical feature that "the upper surface and lower surface of the thermally conductive aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves, and the function of such grooves is to ensure that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation aluminum strips." The judgment of the second instance held that the premise for identifying the textual description "left and right side surfaces" in Claim 2 of this patent regarding the adhesion position of the heat dissipation aluminum strips as a clerical error for "upper and lower surfaces" is that the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in Claim 2 must have grooves, and the function of such grooves is to ensure that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation aluminum strips. Without this premise, correcting the clerical error of "left and right side surfaces" to "upper and lower surfaces" in Claim 2 would lack a basis for argumentation. Therefore, although Claim 2 of this patent does not contain the technical feature that "the upper surface and lower surface of the thermally conductive aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves," it should be considered an implicit technical feature of Claim 2, and the limiting effect of this technical feature on the scope of protection of Claim 2 must be considered. This Court holds that the so-called implicit technical feature in the judgment of the second instance is essentially introducing content that is not explicitly recorded in the claims as a prerequisite for correcting errors when interpreting the meaning of the technical features in the claims. Since introducing content not explicitly recorded in the claims usually further limits the scope of protection of the claims, caution should be exercised in introducing content not explicitly recorded in the claims during claim interpretation. Specifically in this case, the key issue is whether identifying the textual description "left and right side surfaces" regarding the adhesion position of the heat dissipation aluminum strips in Claim 2 of this patent as a clerical error for "upper and lower surfaces" and correcting it is premised on the requirement that "the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in Claim 2 must have grooves, and the function of such grooves is to ensure that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation aluminum strips." First, based on the foregoing discussion that the statement in Claim 2 that the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the "left and right side surfaces" of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core is an obvious error that can be corrected, the identification and correction of this obvious error do not require as a prerequisite that the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in Claim 2 have grooves. Second, the grooves on the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in Claim 1 of this patent and the semi-circular grooves formed on the left and right side surfaces after pressing in Claim 2 serve different functions and are not directly related. In this case, paragraph [0006] of the specification of this patent records that the upper surface and lower surface of the thermally conductive aluminum tube of the PTC heater are respectively provided with grooves; paragraph [0007] records that after pressing, semi-circular grooves are formed on the left side surface and right side surface of the thermally conductive aluminum tube; paragraph [0010] records that the grooves on the surface of the aluminum tube and the semi-circular grooves on the side surfaces of the heating core of the aluminum tube offset the extension of the aluminum tube in the width direction, ensuring that the width of the thermally conductive aluminum tube of the heating core after pressing is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation strips. It can be seen that the semi-circular grooves on the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube are for clamping the heating core, while the grooves on the upper and lower surfaces are for ensuring that the width of the upper and lower surfaces after pressing is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation strips. Therefore, the semi-circular grooves on the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube and the grooves on the upper and lower surfaces of the aluminum tube serve different functions, have no synergistic effect, and neither requires the existence of the other as a prerequisite. Finally, Decision No. 24085, when correcting the obvious error in Claim 2, did not take the existence of grooves on the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube as a prerequisite. In the process of making an interpretive correction to the adhesion position of the heat dissipation aluminum strips in Claim 2, Decision No. 24085 held: "According to the current limitation of Claim 2, after pressing the thermally conductive aluminum tube, semi-circular grooves are formed on the left and right side surfaces and cannot form a flat surface. The heat dissipation aluminum strips cannot be adhered in semi-circular grooves, i.e., the above description of features in Claim 2 is obviously contradictory." It can be seen that the reason for Decision No. 24085 to determine that Claim 2 contained a clerical error was merely that "after pressing the thermally conductive aluminum tube, semi-circular grooves are formed on the left and right side surfaces and cannot form a flat surface," which has no necessary connection to whether the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube are provided with grooves. Therefore, the judgment of the second instance's determination that Claim 2 of this patent implicitly includes the technical feature that "the upper surface and lower surface of the thermally conductive aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves, and the function of such grooves is to ensure that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation aluminum strips" lacks factual basis.

In summary, the judgment of the second instance erred in determining the scope of protection of Claim 2 of this patent. The ground for retrial application of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping on this point is established and should be supported.

(II) Whether the accused infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of Claim 2 of this patent

Claim 2 of this patent can be divided into the following technical features: A PTC heater (Feature A), comprising a heating core (Feature B) and heat dissipation aluminum strips (Feature C); the heating core is formed by pressing ceramic PTC heating elements, insulating ceramic sheets, conductive electrodes, and an insulating layer through the rear cavity of a thermally conductive aluminum tube (Feature D); the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core (Feature E); after pressing, semi-circular grooves are formed on the left side surface and right side surface of the thermally conductive aluminum tube (Feature F).

Considering the defenses raised by Linzhi Company during the original trial, it argued that the accused infringing product differs from the technical features of Claim 2 of this patent in the following aspects: the accused infringing product does not have grooves on the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube, while Claim 2 of this patent specifies that the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves (Difference Feature 1); the heat dissipation aluminum strips of the accused infringing product are fixed to the upper and lower surfaces by brazing or through wedge grooves on the thermally conductive aluminum tube, while in Claim 2, the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube (Difference Feature 2); the grooves on the left and right side surfaces of the accused infringing product are not formed after pressing but are formed before pressing, and the shape of the grooves is an inverted "人" shaped groove or "U"-shaped groove, which differs from the semi-circular grooves of Claim 2 of this patent in terms of formation time, shape, and function (Difference Feature 3); the widths of the thermally conductive aluminum tube and the heat dissipation aluminum strips in the accused infringing product are inconsistent, while Claim 2 of this patent has the implicit technical feature that "the width of the thermally conductive aluminum tube is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation aluminum strips" (Difference Feature 4). In addition, Linzhi Company also argued that the principle of estoppel should apply in this case, as the patentee, during the invalidation proceedings, made a limiting interpretation of the patent claims, emphasizing the differences and advantages of the semi-circular grooves of this patent over the U-shaped grooves in the prior art, which was adopted by the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office, and thus the U-shaped grooves of the accused infringing product are inconsistent with the technical feature of the semi-circular grooves of this patent. The so-called Difference Features 1, 2, and 4 raised by Linzhi Company relate to the interpretation of Claim 2 of this patent; its so-called Difference Feature 3 is closely related to the principle of estoppel it advocates. Accordingly, this Court analyzes as follows:

First, regarding the so-called Difference Features 1 and 4 raised by Linzhi Company. Linzhi Company's so-called Difference Feature 1, "the accused infringing product does not have grooves on the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube," and Difference Feature 4, "the widths of the thermally conductive aluminum tube and the heat dissipation aluminum strips in the accused infringing product are inconsistent," both relate to the "implicit technical features" introduced by the judgment of the second instance for Claim 2 of this patent. As previously stated, the judgment of the second instance's determination that Claim 2 of this patent implicitly includes the technical feature that "the upper surface and lower surface of the thermally conductive aluminum tube are respectively provided with grooves, and the function of such grooves is to ensure that the width of the upper and lower surfaces is consistent with the width of the heat dissipation aluminum strips" lacks factual basis. Claim 2 of this patent does not implicitly include the above technical features. Therefore, the so-called Difference Features 1 and 4 raised by Linzhi Company are not differences between the technical solution of the accused infringing product and Claim 2 of this patent.

Second, regarding the so-called Difference Feature 2 raised by Linzhi Company. Linzhi Company's so-called Difference Feature 2, "the heat dissipation aluminum strips of the accused infringing product are fixed to the upper and lower surfaces by brazing or through wedge grooves on the thermally conductive aluminum tube," relates to Feature E of Claim 2 of this patent, i.e., "the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core." As previously stated, the "left and right side surfaces" in Claim 2 of this patent, which states "the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the left and right side surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core," are indeed a clerical error for "upper and lower surfaces" and should be corrected to "upper and lower surfaces." Therefore, the only difference raised by Linzhi Company lies in the method of fixing the heat dissipation aluminum strips in the accused infringing product, i.e., the heat dissipation aluminum strips of the accused infringing product are "fixed to the upper and lower surfaces by brazing or through wedge grooves on the thermally conductive aluminum tube," while in Feature E of Claim 2 of this patent, the heat dissipation aluminum strips are "adhered" to the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube. This issue involves the interpretation of "adhered" in Feature E of Claim 2 of this patent. The interpretation of patent claims must be based on the perspective of a person skilled in the art and a holistic understanding combining the information provided in the specification. From the description of the purpose of the invention in the specification of this patent, it can be seen that the purpose of this patent is to provide a thermally conductive aluminum tube for a PTC heater with lower cost and more reasonable structure, and a PTC heater with better thermal conductivity and better insulation performance. To achieve this purpose, a person skilled in the art can understand that the heat dissipation aluminum strips being "adhered" to the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in Feature E is to ensure sufficient contact between the heating core and the heat dissipation aluminum strips, so that the heat of the heating core can be efficiently conducted out through the heat dissipation aluminum strips. Therefore, "adhered" here should be understood as "attached," and there is no strict limitation on the manner of achieving attachment between the heating core and the heat dissipation aluminum strips; it may be by welding, wedge groove fixing, adhesive bonding, or other methods. It can be seen that the feature of the accused infringing product that "the heat dissipation aluminum strips are fixed to the upper and lower surfaces by brazing or through wedge grooves on the thermally conductive aluminum tube" constitutes an identical feature to Feature E of Claim 2 of this patent, i.e., "the heat dissipation aluminum strips are adhered to the upper and lower surfaces of the thermally conductive aluminum tube in the heating core."

Third, regarding the so-called distinguishing feature 3 raised by Linzhi Company and the application of the doctrine of estoppel. The so-called distinguishing feature 3 raised by Linzhi Company and the application of the doctrine of estoppel relate to feature F of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit: "after pressing, semicircular grooves are formed on the left side and the right side of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe, respectively." Linzhi Company argued that the grooves on the left and right sides of the accused infringing product were formed before pressing, not after pressing, and that the groove shape was an inverted "V" shaped groove or a "U" shaped groove, which differed from the semicircular groove of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit in terms of formation time, shape, and function. First, regarding the interpretation of feature F of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit. According to the specification of the patent-in-suit, the function of "after pressing, semicircular grooves are formed on the left side and the right side of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe, respectively" is to offset the extension of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe in the width direction during pressing, ensure that the fit clearance between the components inside the cavity of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe and the inner wall of the side face of the aluminum pipe is reduced, and make the product structure more compact. Therefore, the semicircular groove in feature F requires a pressing process, during which an inward deformation occurs, and the semicircular groove is formed after pressing. As to whether there were grooves on the left and right sides of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe before pressing and the shape of such grooves, feature F of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit does not impose any limitation. Second, regarding the formation time and function of the grooves on the left and right sides of the accused infringing product. According to Linzhi Company's statements during the first instance trial, the grooves on the left and right sides of the accused infringing product were pre-formed, but the four corners of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe needed to be pressed, and after pressing, the grooves would further deform, with the purpose of pressing the upper and lower surfaces of the aluminum pipe against the heating core to make them fit more closely. It is evident that even if the grooves on the left and right sides of the accused infringing product were pre-formed, there was still a pressing process, during which the grooves would deform inward, serving to absorb the extension of the aluminum pipe in the width direction during pressing. This is the same function as that of the semicircular groove in feature F of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit. Moreover, feature F of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit does not limit whether there were grooves on the left and right sides of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe before pressing. Third, regarding the shape of the grooves on the left and right sides of the accused infringing product. The shape of the grooves on the left and right sides of the accused infringing product is an inverted "V" shaped groove or a "U" shaped groove. As discussed above, the main function of the "semicircular grooves" formed on the left and right sides of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe after pressing in feature F of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit is to offset the extension of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe in the width direction during pressing, making the product structure more compact. The inverted "V" shaped grooves or "U" shaped grooves on the left and right sides of the accused infringing product also deform during the pressing process, absorbing the extension of the aluminum pipe in the width direction during pressing, and making the product structure more compact. It can be seen that the inverted "V" shaped grooves or "U" shaped grooves on the left and right sides of the accused infringing product have the same function and achieve the same effect as the "semicircular grooves" in feature F. At the same time, both the inverted "V" shaped groove or "U" shaped groove and the semicircular groove absorb the extension of the aluminum pipe in the width direction during pressing by means of inward depression, the means are basically the same, and a person of ordinary skill in the art could conceive of this without creative labor. Therefore, the accused infringing product possesses a feature equivalent to feature F of Claim 2: "after pressing, semicircular grooves are formed on the left side and the right side of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe, respectively." Finally, regarding the application of the so-called doctrine of estoppel raised by Linzhi Company. Based on the facts ascertained by this Court, during the patent invalidation proceedings for the patent-in-suit, the patentee argued that the function of the groove of the patent-in-suit differed from the function of the groove in Evidence 5; the function of the "U", "W", and "V" shaped grooves in Evidence 5 was to fix components, while the function of the semicircular groove of the patent-in-suit was to offset the extension of the aluminum pipe in the width direction during pressing; the groove of the patent-in-suit was formed only after the thermally conductive aluminum pipe was pressed, while the V-shaped groove of Evidence 5 was formed before pressing. Decision No. 24085 recognized the patentee's above argument concerning the different functions of the grooves on the left and right sides of the patent-in-suit compared to the groove in Evidence 5. Regarding the patentee's above argument that the groove of the patent-in-suit was formed only after pressing, while the V-shaped groove of Evidence 5 was formed before pressing, Decision No. 24085 held that since the solution of Evidence 5 could not achieve the operation of pressing the accommodating cavity from the upper and lower surfaces of the shoveled finned heat sink, the structure of Evidence 5 required a "U" shaped groove to be provided before pressing the aluminum pipe to provide a continuously adjustable pressing force, whereas in the patent-in-suit, when the heating element was inserted into the aluminum pipe, the semicircular groove could be temporarily not formed or could be slightly depressed, and the semicircular grooves on the left and right sides of the aluminum pipe were formed after pressing. It can be seen that although the patentee emphasized the function and formation time of the semicircular grooves on the left and right sides of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe of the patent-in-suit during the patent invalidation proceedings, the patentee did not completely exclude the possibility of grooves of a specific shape existing on the left and right sides of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe before pressing. At the same time, Decision No. 24085 clearly affirmed that the left and right sides of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe of the patent-in-suit could have a slight depression before pressing. Therefore, the patentee's statements during the invalidation proceedings did not waive the technical solution in which grooves of a specific shape exist on the left and right sides of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe before pressing, and Decision No. 24085 further affirmed that the patent-in-suit included the technical solution in which grooves of a specific shape exist on the left and right sides of the thermally conductive aluminum pipe before pressing. The patentee's statements during the invalidation proceedings did not give rise to the legal effect of estoppel as alleged by Linzhi Company.

Apart from the above reasons, Linzhi Company did not raise any other differences between the accused infringing product and Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit. Upon review, this Court finds that the accused infringing product possesses the other technical features of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit.

In summary, the accused infringing product in this case possesses technical features identical or equivalent to those of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit, and thus falls within the scope of protection of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit.

(III) Assumption of Civil Liability for Infringement

Since the accused infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit, in accordance with the claims of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping, the respondents Linzhi Company and Suning Company shall bear corresponding civil liability. Regarding the specific form of civil liability, in conjunction with the claims of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping, the analysis and evaluation are as follows:

First, regarding the claim for cessation of infringement. The accused infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit, and Linzhi Company and Suning Company shall bear the civil liability for cessation of infringement. Cessation of the production and sale of infringing products is one of the necessary measures for cessation of infringement. This Court supports the claims of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping for an order that Linzhi Company immediately cease the production and sale of the accused infringing product, and that Suning Company immediately cease the sale of air conditioning units incorporating the infringing product in this case. If Linzhi Company currently holds any of the infringing products in this case, such products shall be destroyed to prevent them from entering the sales channels. This Court supports the claim of Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping for an order that Linzhi Company destroy the infringing products.

Second, regarding the claim for compensation for losses and reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement. Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping requested an order that Linzhi Company compensate for economic losses and reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement, totaling RMB 15,000,000. Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping argued that the damages in this case should be calculated based on the profits gained by Linzhi Company from the infringement. Their calculation method was: total sales amount of the infringing product by Linzhi Company, RMB 169,556,341, multiplied by the profit margin of the infringing product of 15%, yielding an infringement profit of approximately RMB 25,430,000. Based on this, Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping contended that the amount of damages they claimed was reasonable. In this regard, this Court analyzes as follows:

First, regarding the reasonableness of the calculation method for damages claimed by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping. 1. Regarding the total sales amount of the infringing product by Linzhi Company claimed by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping. The total sales amount of the infringing product by Linzhi Company claimed by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping was RMB 169,556,341. This total amount included the supply amounts from Linzhi Company to Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd., the Procurement Department of Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., and the Procurement Department of TCL Air Conditioner Business Division. However, the evidence provided by Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd., the Procurement Department of Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., and the Procurement Department of TCL Air Conditioner Business Division did not show that the entire supply amount represented the supply amount of the accused infringing product in this case. At the same time, this total product sales amount included both amounts including tax (for example, the amounts for the Hisense Pingdu Base and Huzhou Base were amounts including tax) and amounts excluding tax (for example, the amounts for the Hisense Shunde Base and Jiangmen Base were amounts excluding tax). Therefore, the total sales amount of the infringing product by Linzhi Company claimed by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping was not accurate. 2. Regarding the calculation method for damages claimed by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping. Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping argued that the damages should be calculated by multiplying the total sales amount of the infringing product by the profit margin of the infringing product. The total sales amount of the infringing product multiplied by the profit margin of the infringing product yields the sales profit of the infringing product, which is not necessarily the profit obtained by the infringer from the infringement. The reason is that the profit from the accused infringing product may come not only from the use of the patented technical solution but also from other patents or other components used. Therefore, the contribution of the patent-in-suit to the profit of the infringing product needs to be considered. In view of this, this Court will consider the calculation method for damages claimed by Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping after eliminating the influence of the above unreasonable factors.

Secondly, regarding the calculation of the total sales amount of Linzhi Company's infringing product. Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping submitted evidence of the supply quantities and amounts of Linzhi Company's supplies to Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd., the Procurement Department of Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., and the Procurement Department of TCL Air Conditioner Business Division. 1. Regarding the evidence of Linzhi Company's supplies to Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd., the Procurement Department of Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., and the Procurement Department of TCL Air Conditioner Business Division. Although the evidence of Linzhi Company's supplies issued by Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd. and the Procurement Department of TCL Air Conditioner Business Division recorded material codes, it was still difficult to determine the proportion of the accused infringing product in this case within the supply quantity based solely on these codes. The evidence issued by the Procurement Department of Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd. only recorded the supply amount, and it was similarly difficult to determine the proportion of the accused infringing product in this case. Therefore, this Court finds it difficult to use these three pieces of evidence as the benchmark basis for calculating the amount of damages based on the method of profit gained from infringement. For these three pieces of evidence, this Court will determine the amount of damages in accordance with the statutory compensation method. 2. Regarding the evidence of Linzhi Company's supplies to Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd. Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd. not only provided evidence of the supply quantities and amounts for nine models of products supplied by Linzhi Company but also provided physical evidence for seven related models, and clearly stated that all nine models had no difference in the aluminum tube structure of the heating element. In the absence of contrary evidence provided by Linzhi Company, this Court presumes that the product quantities and sales amounts of Linzhi Company's supplies provided by Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd. are the quantities and sales amounts of the infringing product in this case. According to the evidence provided by Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., from 2011 to 2015, Linzhi Company supplied nine models of electric heaters to Hisense's four bases (Pingdu, Huzhou, Shunde, and Jiangmen). The total supply amount for the Pingdu Base and Huzhou Base was RMB 125,755,180.53 (including tax), and the total supply amount for the Shunde Base and Jiangmen Base was RMB 6,688,496.74 (excluding tax). Since the total sales amount of Linzhi Company's supplies provided by Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd. included both the amounts including tax for the Hisense Pingdu Base and Huzhou Base and the amounts excluding tax for the Hisense Shunde Base and Jiangmen Base, the amounts including tax for the Hisense Pingdu Base and Huzhou Base should be converted to amounts excluding tax. According to Article 2 of the Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Value Added Tax (effective January 1, 2009), as a production and processing enterprise, the VAT rate payable by Linzhi Company was 17%. After deducting the corresponding VAT, the total sales amount (excluding tax) of Linzhi Company's sales of the infringing product in this case to Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd. was approximately RMB 114,371,557.

Thirdly, regarding the profit margin of Linzhi Company's sales of the infringing product. During the first instance trial of this case, Linzhi Company stated that the profit margin of its products was approximately 10%-15%. According to the "Report on the Verification of Enterprise Information Disclosure for Wuxi Guowei Ceramic Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. for 2014" issued by Yixing Zhengda Tax Agent Firm of Jiangsu Province, among the 12 products of Guowei Company, the lowest sales profit margin was 16.54% and the highest was 32.04%. Taking into comprehensive consideration the highest profit margin claimed by Linzhi Company and the lowest profit margin claimed by Guowei Company, this Court determines the profit margin of the accused infringing product to be 15%.

Finally, regarding the contribution of the patent-in-suit to the profit of the infringing product. According to the description of the beneficial effects of the invention in the specification of the patent-in-suit, the beneficial effects related to the technical solution of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit include a more compact product structure, a stronger bond between components after pressing, improved thermal conductivity, reduced safety hazards caused by loose components, and improved product reliability and manufacturing cost. It can be seen that the patent-in-suit played an important role in the market appeal of Linzhi Company's PTC heaters. At the same time, considering that the features of the technical solution of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit that achieve the above beneficial effects are primarily reflected in the semicircular groove structure formed on the left and right sides after pressing the thermally conductive aluminum pipe, and that the PTC heater includes other components, it is inappropriate to attribute the entire profit of the infringing product to the patent-in-suit. In the absence of a legitimate reason for Linzhi Company's refusal to participate in the trial of this case, this Court determines that the contribution rate of the patent-in-suit to the profit of Linzhi Company's infringing product is 50%.

Based on the above analysis, this Court calculates the profit obtained by Linzhi Company from infringing the patent-in-suit in the process of selling the accused infringing product to Hisense (Shandong) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd. as follows: RMB 114,371,557 x 15% x 50% = RMB 8,577,867.

Third, regarding the calculation of damages for Linzhi Company's supply activities to Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd., the Procurement Department of Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., and the Procurement Department of TCL Air Conditioner Business Division. As discussed above, since the existing evidence is insufficient to prove the proportion of the accused infringing product in this case in Linzhi Company's total sales to the above three entities, the losses caused to Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping by Linzhi Company's sales activities to the above three entities, and the profits gained by Linzhi Company from the infringement, are both difficult to determine, and there is no reasonable patent license fee available for reference. This Court will determine the amount of damages for Linzhi Company's sales of the accused infringing product in this case to the above three entities in accordance with statutory compensation. Considering that the patent-in-suit is a utility model patent, and that Linzhi Company engaged in the production and sale of the accused infringing product on a relatively large scale, this Court determines that Linzhi Company shall compensate the patentees Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping for economic losses in the amount of RMB 800,000 for its sales activities to Guangdong Midea Refrigeration Equipment Co., Ltd., the Procurement Department of Hisense (Zhejiang) Air Conditioning Co., Ltd., and the Procurement Department of TCL Air Conditioner Business Division.

Fourth, regarding the reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement. During the first instance proceedings of this case, to obtain the accused infringing product in this case, Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping purchased three air conditioners by notarized purchase: a TCL air conditioner with a total price of RMB 1,699, a Hisense air conditioner with a total price of RMB 2,799, and a Midea air conditioner with a total price of RMB 2,299, totaling RMB 6,797. Apart from the above evidence collection expenses supported by corresponding invoices, Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping did not provide corresponding vouchers to prove the expenses incurred for entrusting notarization, entrusting investigation and evidence collection, and entrusting lawyers to participate in the litigation of this case. Nevertheless, considering the actual circumstances of this case, it was reasonable and necessary for Guowei Company and Jiang Guoping to entrust notarization, investigation, evidence collection, and lawyers to participate in this litigation. Since the acts of entrusting notarization, investigation, evidence collection, and lawyers to participate in the litigation have already occurred, corresponding expenses must have been incurred. This Court will support the notarization fees, investigation and evidence collection fees, and attorney fees on a discretionary basis. Based on the circumstances of this case, this Court determines that Linzhi Company shall compensate the patentees for reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringement in the amount of RMB 60,000.

In summary, the interpretation of the scope of protection of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit in the second-instance judgment was improper. Based on this interpretation, it was erroneous to determine that the accused infringing product did not fall within the scope of protection of Claim 2 of the patent-in-suit, and the ruling result was incorrect and should be corrected. Although the conclusion of the first-instance judgment that Linzhi Company constituted infringement of the patent-in-suit was correct, applying statutory compensation to determine the amount of damages when some evidence in this case could prove the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement constituted an error in the application of law and should be corrected. 1. The civil judgment (2016) Su Min Zhong No. 105 of the Jiangsu High People's Court is vacated;

2. Items 1, 2, and 4 of the civil judgment (2013) Ning Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 510 of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province are affirmed;

3. Item 3 of the civil judgment (2013) Ning Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 510 of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province is amended to: "Changshu Linzhi Electric Heating Device Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Wuxi Guowei Ceramic Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. and Jiang Guoping for economic losses in the amount of RMB 9,377,867, and for reasonable expenses incurred in stopping the infringing act in the amount of RMB 60,000, totaling RMB 9,437,867."
